Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Here’s a simple starting point:
Vodka — clean and subtle; great in cocktails because it lets mixers shine.
Rum — often smoother and a little sweeter; ideal for cocktails, with some styles enjoyable neat.
Whiskey — richer and more layered; lower-proof bottles around 40% ABV can feel gentler, with softer fruit or floral notes.
Gin — botanical and aromatic, often with juniper and citrus-like notes.
Tequila — made from agave; can range from bright and fresh to richer, oak-aged styles.
For an easy first choice, vodka or rum are approachable cocktail bases, while a gentler whiskey can be a good introduction to sipping spirits.

turns.q: How do I use it properly the very first time?
turns.replyTail:
Daiquiri—it’s an easy way to taste the rum without drinking it straight:
Add 2 parts rum, 1 part freshly squeezed lime juice, and 2 teaspoons sugar to a jar or shaker.
Add cubed ice, seal, and shake until cold.
Pour into a glass; add a lime wedge if you like.
If you prefer something fruitier, fill a glass with ice, add 2 oz rum, 6 oz orange juice, and 1 oz grenadine.
